## 작업 요약

인증 및 권한 관리 시스템 개선과 신고 확인 모달 구현을 통해 사용자 경험과 보안을 강화했습니다. 인증 상태 확인부터 관리자 권한 검증, 소유자 확인까지 체계적인 권한 관리 시스템을 구축하고, 신고 프로세스에 확인 단계를 추가하여 허위 신고를 방지하도록 했습니다.

close #31

### 해당 PR에 영향 받는 코드 및 담당자

- 인증/권한 관련 모든 컴포넌트: 전체 팀 (`components/`, `lib/auth.tsx`)
- 신고 시스템: @관리자 담당자 (`components/report-modal.tsx`, `components/admin/`)

### PR 타입

- [x] 기능 구현(요구 사항 변경으로 인한 수정 포함)
- [x] 코드 리팩토링
- [x] 문제 해결(Fix)

## 작업 설명

### AS-IS

- **인증 관리**: 각 컴포넌트마다 인증 로직이 중복되어 있음
- **권한 확인**: Admin 페이지 접근 시 실제 admin 권한 확인 부족
- **소유자 확인**: 게시글/댓글 작성자 확인 로직이 분산되어 있음
- **신고 시스템**: 바로 신고 접수되어 실수로 신고하는 경우 발생 가능
- **UI 일관성**: 버튼 크기와 스타일이 일관되지 않음
- **로딩 상태**: API 호출 중 로딩 표시 부족

### TO-BE

- **통합 인증 시스템**: HOC 패턴으로 인증 로직 통합 관리
- **다층 권한 가드**: AdminOnlyRoute, AuthRequiredRoute로 세분화된 권한 관리
- **신고 확인 프로세스**: 2단계 신고 프로세스로 허위 신고 방지
- **일관된 UI**: 모든 버튼 컴포넌트 스타일 통일
- **향상된 UX**: 로딩 상태와 에러 처리 개선

#### 주요 구현 사항

1. **권한 가드 컴포넌트**
   - `AdminOnlyRoute`: 관리자만 접근 가능
   -  `AuthRequiredRoute`: 회원만 접근 가능

2. **신고 확인 모달**
   - `ReportConfirmModal`: 신고 실행 전 최종 확인
   - 2단계 프로세스: 사유 선택 → 확인 → 신고 접수
   - 허위 신고 방지 메시지 포함

3. **타입 안정성 개선**
   - 소유자 확인을 위한 타입 정의 강화

### 이번 PR에서 하지 않는 것과 해당 내용에 대한 앞으로의 PR 계획

- HOC를 활용한 추가 컴포넌트 래핑 (기존 컴포넌트의 점진적 적용 예정)
- 권한별 세부 메뉴 표시/숨김 기능 (추후 UI/UX 개선 PR에서 진행 예정)

## 리뷰 요구사항

- (필수) #31 이슈에 나와 있는 인증/권한 관리 문제를 해결했는지
- 권한 가드 컴포넌트들이 적절히 권한을 체크하고 있는지
- 신고 확인 모달이 사용자 경험을 해치지 않으면서도 허위 신고를 방지하는지
- 타입 안정성이 보장되는지 (특히 `authorId` 관련)
- 로딩 상태와 에러 처리가 적절한지

### 검증 방법

**인증/권한 테스트:**
1. 비로그인 상태에서 admin 페이지 접근 시도 → 접근 차단 확인
2. 일반 사용자로 admin 페이지 접근 시도 → 접근 차단 확인
3. 관리자 계정으로 admin 페이지 접근 → 정상 접근 확인
4. 다른 사용자의 게시글 수정 시도 → 접근 차단 확인

**신고 시스템 테스트:**
1. 게시글 신고 버튼 클릭 → 사유 선택 → 확인 모달 표시 → 최종 신고 확인
2. 확인 모달에서 취소 → 신고 취소 확인
3. 신고 완료 후 토스트 메시지 확인

### 참고 문서

- [ERD](https://www.erdcloud.com/d/YkLd3DqEqkiCBwCkt)

## 기타

- 권한 가드 컴포넌트들은 재사용성을 고려하여 설계했습니다
- 신고 확인 모달은 AlertDialog를 사용하여 사용자의 주의를 끌도록 구현했습니다
- 모든 권한 체크는 클라이언트와 서버 양쪽에서 검증되도록 설계했습니다

author: domosoftdev
body:
This commit consolidates all the features developed for the Web Security Checker tool.

It includes:
- **Multiple Report Formats:** Adds support for generating reports in HTML, CSV, and JSON formats using the `--formats` command-line argument.
- **Vulnerability Database Integration:** The JavaScript library scanner now queries the OSV.dev database to find specific, known vulnerabilities (CVEs) for outdated libraries, and includes them in the reports.
- **In-depth WordPress Scans:** A new module performs WordPress-specific checks if the target is identified as a WordPress site. This includes checking for exposed configuration files, user enumeration vulnerabilities, and enumerating installed plugins.
- **Scoring System:** A risk scoring system has been implemented to provide an overall grade (A+ to F) based on the severity of the findings.
- **Targeted Remediation:** The tool now provides targeted remediation advice based on the detected server technology (e.g., Nginx, Apache).

## Description
Previously we were just saving when a notification was sent, its message id and checkout id. Those fields don't define a report, so we weren't able to discern if a specific report had been sent or not. This knowledge is useful in order to be able to not query for all reports all the time, allowing us to skip heavy reports and only re-send them after some time.

## Changes
- Added more fields to the NotificationCheckouts table in order to identify a unique report
  - Updates old entries with a specific `RunPython` migration piece
- Added check to see which reports where sent in the last 12 hours (possible to change with a global variable)
- Added ability to skip reports that were already sent in that interval, defaulted to true

## How to test
- Run the migration with `poetry run python3 manage.py migrate --database=notifications`
- Run the summary command with `poetry run python3 manage.py notifications --action summary`
- Mock the "mark as sent" by commenting the line with `if msg_id and email_args.update` and let some reports be marked as sent with whatever msg_id
- Run the summary command again, this time you'll see a log saying that some of the reports were skipped due to being already sent recently

body:
This is my first PR to three.js.

When using the Ascii Effect, I thought it'd be nice to be able to use a user-specified font and to pass in a post-processed render as input (instead of the bare render only). This PR is mainly focused on achieving those two things.

### Exhaustive changelog ~(at time of first commit)~:

- Moved `charSet` inside the constructor options.
  - I understand this might be a breaking change, in which case that would not be accepted, but I believe it makes sense. Previously, you had to input a charSet to be able to set the options (unless I'm mistaken, not yet a Javascript pro). Now, you don't have to specify it to access the other options, but you can.
- Added `fontFamily`, `fontWeight`, `fontSize` and `letterSpacing` options. `fontFamily` and `fontWeight` are because they're the main goal of this PR, but it turns out that monospace fonts' characters are rarely fitting in a perfect square: if the user adds a custom `fontFamily`, they'll want to customize `letterSpacing`, otherwise the output might be squished/stretched.
- ~Added `composer` as an option, allowing to pass a post-processed render as input of the Ascii Effect, instead of the bare render only.~
- Updated the logic accordingly.
- ~Updated the example page with `UnrealBloomPass` to show the newly added option.~
- Set the canvas pixelRatio to the AsciiEffect's for performance gain.

### Possible mistakes to look out for (my first three.js PR)

- `strFontSize` defaults to `'Dynamically computed according to resolution'`. This allows for logic check later, but might be misinterpreted by users/LLMs trying to use the effect.
- Incorrect JSDoc usage, type checking, etc.
- Breaking change by moving `charSet` inside the constructor options.

Added configurable OTP options through environment variables to allow administrators to control which contact methods are available:

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_EMAIL_OTP` - Enable/disable email OTP (default: true)
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_PHONE_OTP` - Enable/disable phone OTP (default: false) 
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_CONTACT_METHOD` - Set default contact method (default: email)

Created a new utility `src/lib/otp-config.ts` to manage configuration and updated `OfferGenerator` to conditionally render contact method toggles. **By default, only email is shown as requested.**

## 🎨 Fixed Logo Positioning on Desktop

Resolved the issue where the large logo was causing the form to appear halfway down the viewport, requiring users to scroll:

- Made the `WaffleLogo` responsive with medium size and 75% scale on desktop (`md:scale-75`)

Desktop users can now see the entire form without scrolling while maintaining the visual impact on mobile devices.

author: sporiff
body:
Following discussions on Matrix, I put together this summary of how GUIDs should be calculated using namespaces. This document currently sits outside of the specification hierarchy, but can be divided up into the relevant specs at a later date.

The goal of this document is to set out a normalized approach for calculating GUIDs using predefined namespaces. To put it shortly:

1. The client MUST be responsible for calculating the GUID.
2. Feed GUIDs MUST be parsed from the `guid` tag if present, or calculated by combining the feed URL and the global podcast namespace (`ead4c236-bf58-58c6-a2c6-a6b28d128cb6`).
3. Episode GUIDs MUST be calculated using the calculated feed GUID and EITHER:
  1. The normalized (trimmed) `guid` tag for the episode if available OR
  2. The normalized (lowercased and trimmed) combination of `title`, `enclosure_url`, and `publish_date`, in that order.

The result is a consistent calculation of UUID values that will match across all client implementations. This has the added benefit of reducing the amount of database storage used on the server side as duplicate feeds/episodes can be avoided, and instead users can simply be linked to existing entries. Similarly, it makes the data more portable between different OPA hosts.

I'd like some input specifically regarding my assumption about the metadata used in the podcast episodes.

- Are these values always present?
- How well would this work with client deduplication methods?

author: mrodm
body:
This PR fixes the results given by the `/search` endpoint when the query parameter `category=<category>` is set.

To keep the same behavior this filtering cannot be done at database level, since packages must be filtered by the category once all the other filters have been processed.

https://github.com/elastic/package-registry/blob/d0337e5ac884897bfef1f03e332c259018e00535/packages/packages.go#L516-L517

Doing this filter at database level could return unexpected packages. For instance with the request `/search?category=observability`, it should return the latest packages which category is `observability`.

It could happen that some old version of package contains the `observability` category, but the latest version do not. In that scenario, if this filtering is done at database level, it will return the old package that it should not.

Tests have been updated to take into account this scenario.

author: zmb3
body:
The addition of the issuer SKID to the CN for our CRLS  has caused long clusters to exceed the limit of how long a CN can be.

For database access, we rely on the user to run certutil commands to publish the CRL. While we expect the limit to be 64 characters, we observe that certutil starts truncating the CN as soon as it exceeds 51 characters (which causes it to get imported in a different location from what the certificate references).

Note: no changelog because this will land in the same release as #57822 and one changelog entry is enough to cover both fixes.
